subject.title: feat(models): make per-agent model allowlist explicit; aliases/defaults no longer restrict

question: What authoritative signal should distinguish a shipped implicit `agents.defaults.models` restriction from a current user-edited metadata map that has not yet received the migration marker?
rationale: The same markerless shape represents both legacy restricted installations and ordinary manual configuration edits, so automation cannot choose between preserving legacy restrictions and honoring the new no-implicit-restriction contract without maintainer policy.

options.title: Require an explicit migration boundary
options.body: Recommended: preserve old restrictions only through a versioned/config-load migration or explicit Doctor path, then have runtime consume only canonical `modelPolicy.allow`.

options.title: Keep markerless maps restrictive
options.body: Retain the current fail-closed reader and document that direct edits must run Doctor or a managed config write before aliases and metadata become non-restrictive.

options.title: Make markerless maps unrestricted
options.body: Honor the new semantics immediately for manual configs, accepting that old restricted configurations can become less restrictive before migration.

recommendation.title: Require an explicit migration boundary
recommendation.body: Recommended: preserve old restrictions only through a versioned/config-load migration or explicit Doctor path, then have runtime consume only canonical `modelPolicy.allow`.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and are assigned to the proposed migration and model-policy design.
